data.title: STOCKS | Lyft Airport Pickups Rose by Double Digits During US Flight Grounding
data.description: Lyft Inc. airport pickups rose by double digits during the US flight ground stop last Friday, as stranded passengers turned to ground transportation, including longer-distance rides, to get home or reach their destinations, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: AI TRENDS | Quilter Cheviot: Anthropic's Strong Debut Faces Volatility and Regulatory Risks
data.description: According to Jin10, Ben Ballinger, head of technology research at Quilter Cheviot, said Anthropic performed strongly on its first day of trading, with its shares closing up more than 17%. As initial market enthusiasm fades, the shares could see greater volatility over the coming weeks. Ballinger said Anthropic is well positioned but may not avoid market volatility sweeping the industry after the U.S. midterm elections. He also said Anthropic's models remain at an early stage and the company needs to avoid pushing for excessive regulation that could stifle its growth.

data.title: AI | Lise Buyer Says Companies Must Resemble Anthropic to Trade Like It
data.description:
Lise Buyer said companies seeking to trade like Anthropic need to resemble it. Buyer, founder of Class V Group and one of the chief architects of Google’s 2004 auction IPO, cautioned investors against relying on market chatter, saying a company’s value is ultimately what investors are willing to pay, Bloomberg reported.

Buyer discussed Anthropic’s stronger-than-expected IPO demand, share count and pricing after reports had suggested a possible downsizing.

data.title: AI | Robinhood CIO Discusses Retail Access to Anthropic’s Record-Breaking IPO
data.description:
Robinhood Markets Chief Investment Officer Stephanie Guild said customers continued to buy Nvidia on a net basis on days the stock fell following recent news, even as some customers sold. Nvidia remained one of the platform’s highest-volume stocks, Bloomberg reported.

Guild also discussed Anthropic’s record-breaking IPO, retail access and what the offering says about the AI trade.

data.title: Nvidia to Attend UBS Global Technology and AI Conference on December 1
data.description: According to Jin10, Nvidia announced that it will attend the 30th UBS Global Technology and AI Conference and deliver a speech at 6:35 on December 1 (U.S. Pacific Time), or 22:35 (UTC+8).

data.title: AI | GIC Sees Anthropic Developing “Intelligence Factories”
data.description: GIC remains invested in Anthropic after backing the AI company through multiple private rounds and its blockbuster IPO, according to Bloomberg. Chris Emanuel, head of GIC’s technology investment group, sees Anthropic as part of a broader “reindustrialization” built around intelligence. He said GIC backs category-defining technology companies before, during and after they go public.

data.title: Billionaire Namdar's Firm Acquires Destiny USA Debt
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Namdar Realty Group acquired the debt on Destiny USA, New York state's largest shopping center. The Long Island-based real estate firm is known for distressed retail real estate deals.

data.title: U.S. Treasuries Rise as Yield Curve Steepens, Short-End Bonds Lead
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, U.S. Treasury yields fell in a bull-steepening move on Thursday, led by short- and intermediate-term debt, as a retreat in U.S. stocks and a steady debut for Anthropic PBC failed to sustain confidence in the AI trade. Yields across maturities were near their session lows late in the day as stocks extended losses ahead of the close. Treasury options trading was active, with investors favoring protection against a rally over the coming weeks.

Short-end yields fell by as much as 4 basis points shortly after 3 p.m. U.S. Eastern Time, while long-end yields also edged lower. The 2-year/10-year and 5-year/30-year yield spreads widened by 1.5 basis points and 2 basis points, respectively. The 10-year Treasury yield was around 5.04%, down 3 basis points from Wednesday’s close. The S&P 500 fell 2% and the Nasdaq 100 dropped 2.2% at the close.

Breakeven inflation rates showed little reaction to a solid auction of $19 billion in 10-year inflation-protected Treasuries. The auction’s yield was slightly below the when-issued trading level, and primary dealers received 6% of the offering, the lowest share since July 2025. Long-dated U.S. dollar swap spreads continued to narrow, with the 30-year spread down about 0.5 basis point for a fourth consecutive session. Six issuers sold a combined $15.2 billion in dollar bonds, including Citigroup, which issued $6.5 billion in three tranches.

data.title: Steve Grasso Advises Waiting for a Discount Before Buying Anthropic
data.description: According to CNBC, Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share Wednesday night, above its expected range of $70 to $78, ahead of trading Thursday. Perpetual futures markets indicated the stock may open 15%-20% higher. Steve Grasso, CEO of Grasso Global, said he expects shares to open 10% or 15% above $83, then level off, with a possible selloff in the next couple of days; he advised investors to wait for a lower price rather than buy all at once. Anthropic generated $17 billion in revenue in the third quarter, up from $1.4 billion a year earlier, an increase of more than 1,100%. Its annualized revenue run rate reached $81 billion, and the number of customers spending more than $100,000 annually rose from roughly 1,500 to nearly 12,000 in a year. Grasso cautioned that slower growth could disappoint investors paying a premium for the shares.

data.title: Jensen Huang Foundation Plans $350 Million CoreWeave Compute Rental
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, a foundation established by Jensen Huang and his wife plans to spend $350 million to rent computing capacity from cloud provider CoreWeave. Tax filings show that $108.3 million has already been spent. CoreWeave said the computing capacity will be provided to researchers funded by the foundation.

data.description: According to Jin10, market sources say Apple (AAPL.O) is developing an autonomous AI agent to compete with OpenAI and Anthropic.

data.title: AI | Lightspeed’s Duesterhoeft on Anthropic Bet and AI Model Competition
data.description: Lightspeed Venture Partners’ Sebastian Duesterhoeft said the firm adapted to generative AI’s rapid rise and described backing Anthropic as one of its boldest bets, according to Bloomberg. He discussed lessons from the DeepSeek moment, Anthropic’s focus on developing AI safely and his view that competition among multiple leading AI models could ultimately strengthen the industry.

data.title: P&G Plans to Cut Manufacturing and Logistics Workforce by Up to 30% by 2030
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, Procter & Gamble plans to reduce its manufacturing and logistics workforce by 20% to 30% by the end of the decade amid rising price pressures. Chief Product Supply Officer Luc Reynaert announced the latest cost-saving measures at an investor presentation on Thursday; the workforce reduction will also include contractors.

The maker of Tide laundry detergent and Gillette razor blades aims to save a cumulative $10 billion by 2030 through improved production efficiency. It has been contending with rising oil prices and weak consumer demand as inflation prompts consumers to cut some purchases.

In a May 2025 filing, P&G said about 52,000 employees across roughly 35 countries were responsible for producing its products.

data.title: STOCKS | MSCI to Add Anthropic (ANT.O) to Global Standard Index on December 1
data.description: According to Jin10, MSCI will add Anthropic (ANT.O) to the Global Standard Index, effective December 1.

data.title: Intuit to Sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68 Billion
data.description: According to CNBC, Intuit agreed Thursday to sell Mailchimp to Italian technology company Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion in cash and stock, with the deal set to close in early 2027. Intuit paid $12 billion for Mailchimp in 2021. For its fiscal first quarter, which ended Oct. 31, Intuit reported adjusted earnings of $2.91 per share on $4.35 billion in revenue, above analysts’ estimates of $2.70 per share and $4.31 billion. Mailchimp revenue fell 1% to $313 million. Intuit forecast fiscal 2027 adjusted earnings of $22.88 to $23.12 per share and revenue of $23.081 billion to $23.365 billion, below analysts’ estimates. Intuit shares fell 15% in extended trading.

data.title: Gap Names Ashley Kechter Athleta CEO, Cuts Full-Year Guidance
data.description: According to CNBC, Gap Inc. named Ashley Kechter president and CEO of Athleta, effective Dec. 14, and lowered its full-year outlook. Gap now expects net sales to be roughly flat, versus previous guidance for growth of 1% to 1.5%, and adjusted earnings per share of $2.29 to $2.34, down from $2.35 to $2.45. In fiscal third-quarter results, adjusted earnings per share were 82 cents, above the 78 cents analysts expected, while revenue of $4.01 billion missed the $4.02 billion estimate; comparable sales were flat. Athleta net sales fell 14% to $220 million, and comparable sales declined 15%. CEO Richard Dickson attributed much of the lowered guidance to warmer weather in the quarter’s first two weeks and said Gap expects a meaningful acceleration in shopping ahead of the peak holiday season.

data.title: 42 Macro Founder Sees Sharp Fed Easing in 2027, a Strong Year for Bitcoin
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing Bitcoin Magazine, 42 Macro founder and CEO Darius Dale said sharp, unexpected Federal Reserve easing in 2027 or later remains a likely possibility and agreed that 2027 could be a strong year for Bitcoin. He rejected the view that the Fed has made a policy error despite markets pricing in a December rate hike, saying 42 Macro’s model shows the U.S. economy is far from recession. Dale described the economy as booming and said inflation, a lagging indicator of growth, remains above the Fed’s desired level. He also discussed an AI-driven productivity boom, the possibility of an agreement between the Fed and Treasury, and Bitcoin as a “canary in the liquidity coal mine.” Dale said markets could be choppy over the next few months but remained bullish on 2027.

data.title: AI | Ann Berry Says Claude Users Are Eager to Invest in Anthropic
data.description: Ann Berry, founder and managing partner of Threadneedle, said the opportunity to turn Claude users’ behavior into an investment opportunity creates a “different kind of buzz” around Anthropic, Bloomberg reported. She said Anthropic and its Claude model are continuing to take share from companies such as Microsoft and shift users away from traditional search engines.
